concerns.location: plan.md:§ Implementation Plan – paragraph describing Wilcoxon tests (lines 31‑34)
concerns.text: The plan conducts Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests on F1‑scores across only five random seeds and then applies Benjamini‑Hochberg correction to seven comparisons. With n=5 paired observations the smallest two‑sided p‑value is ≈0.0625, so the declared significance threshold (BH‑adjusted p < 0.05) is unattainable, making the statistical inference invalid.

The deterministic ≤5 000‑node subsampling rule *always* retains all anomalous nodes and the top‑10 % highest‑degree nodes before random sampling. This preferential retention can bias the graph topology toward anomalies, inflating the GCN’s ability to detect them and confounding the comparison with baselines.

During temporal hold‑out, test‑set flows that involve IPs not present in the training graph are simply dropped. Dropping unseen nodes (which may include anomalous IPs) can systematically alter the class distribution in the test set, leading to optimistic precision/recall estimates.

The entire experimental pipeline is evaluated on a single verified dataset (NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3). Claiming that GNNs “improve anomaly detection” without any external validation limits causal inference to this dataset and risks overgeneralization.
